<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/templates/auth-templates.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **19** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2bcaefba91b746c1a43066352b5bd4d319519c35` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `3553aec4d27bf0ffda40eb39af2992093c37c4ef` — the merge of head `bc00a6e504408f48f06839a395ef89972759a117` into base `2bcaefba91b746c1a43066352b5bd4d319519c35`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 3553aec4d27bf0ffda40eb39af2992093c37c4ef && git checkout 3553aec4d27bf0ffda40eb39af2992093c37c4ef
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 2bcaefba91b746c1a43066352b5bd4d319519c35 bc00a6e504408f48f06839a395ef89972759a117 && git checkout -B drift-repro 2bcaefba91b746c1a43066352b5bd4d319519c35 && git merge --no-ff bc00a6e504408f48f06839a395ef89972759a117

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2bcaefba91b746c1a43066352b5bd4d319519c35
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 2bcaefba91b746c1a43066352b5bd4d319519c35` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `bc00a6e504408f48f06839a395ef89972759a117`
Local-runs: none

Owed by the `Clause-②: yes (widening)` declaration alone: the claim `6235666553` was amended in place, with record `6236653214` on #24154. The diff touches no `packages/spec/src/**` file and no governed path. Read: the diff, the card and its thread, and this head's check-runs, at 2026-10-17T16:29Z.

### ① Derived judgments

- **`AuthManagerOptions.getI18n?: () => II18nService | undefined`, a widening and correct.** `plugin-auth/src/index.ts` re-exports `./auth-manager.js` whole, so the optional member is published. It is optional, so every existing caller compiles unchanged. It has one producer, `AuthPlugin.init`, which wires it lazily from `ctx.getService('i18n')` and answers `undefined` when that service is unregistered. It has one reader, the `auth.invitation` send. It takes the shape of the existing lazy accessors `getTenancy` and `getAuditSink`. No existing option reaches the i18n service, as read on `main`. The narrower spellings (a setter, a constructor argument) add a published member all the same.
- **`invitationRoleLabel` is not published.** It lives in its own module, `src/invitation-role-label.ts`, and `index.ts` does not re-export it: 33 export lines read, no hit. It is imported by `auth-manager.ts` only.
- **`{{role}}` now carries a label where it carried the stored value.** This is a value, not a type: the variable keeps its name and `type: 'string'`, and gains a `description`. No published text said it was the stored value. The behaviour change for an embedder that overrode `auth.invitation` is stated in the changeset ("it now receives the label, not the stored value"). That is a stated change, not a silent one.
- **The four `auth.invitation` text bodies gain the role clause.** Template content, not a contract shape. The HTML bodies' render-identity digests are unchanged.
- **The locale rule is unchanged.** It is the recipient's stored locale, then the deployment default, and the inviter's request is never used. `emailLocaleArg(undefined, storedLocale)` is the same call, moved above the `try` so that the label and the send read one value.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/plugin-auth` `minor` (a new optional public option) and `@objectstack/plugin-email` `patch` (template text and a variable description). Both match the diff. The changeset carries `Clause-②: yes (widening)` at a line start, as does the PR body.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **The dev's one open question** (keep `yes`/`minor`, revert to `no`, or change the reach) is ruled by the seat at `6236653214`: keep. Reverting would contradict the built declarations, and a different reach is still a published member.
- **The dev's Acceptance note** (a locale with no shipped template row renders the `en-US` row, while the label follows that locale's i18n chain) is a stated boundary that the console shares. It is not a flag.
- No other flag is raised.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-24154-invitation-role-label`
Reviewed-by: `session_01Nk17Z26X5DB59iQztDBADH`

**VERDICT: PASS**

It splits a comma role list and joins the labels with `Intl.ListFormat`, probed. A token with no label is named as stored, with one warn. On an i18n failure it uses the authored labels with one warn.
